One of the most honest reads on enterprise AI returns⬇️

Jane Street just raised $14.6B in senior secured notes, the largest bond deal ever by a non-bank market maker. The 10-year tranche priced at 8.088%. Primarily a refi of a $5.5B floater and an $11B debt load, but tech infrastructure and trading expansion are stated uses.

What makes this rare: Jane Street is one of the largest disclosed non-tech internal-GPU users, and one of the few with publicly priced debt against it: 4,032 liquid-cooled GPUs in Dallas, ~$6B committed to CoreWeave plus $1B of equity, early work on a self-financed 100-200MW build, targeting 10x into the hundreds of thousands.

They sell no compute and no inference. The chips forecast asset prices. The output is directly monetized and the funding cost is observable.

So, the bar is computable: At CRWV's 6-year depreciation life and 10% salvage, $100 of Jane Street capex must throw off $20.33 (20.3%) annually for six years plus $10 back at the end to set NPV at zero against 8%, 10-year money.

Salvage assumptions barely move it. Every 10 points of recovery buys only ~136bp annually: 25% salvage requires an 18.3% cash yield, etc.

So Jane Street is carrying 8% money against a ~20% break-even, even on modest salvage assumptions. Nobody with their track record takes that trade casually, a real signal about what monetized AI output can earn when someone can actually measure it.

It's also a signal about what the bond market will underwrite: $14.6B, ten years out against a "six-year asset," no NVIDIA residual backstop, clearing on conservative salvage assumptions. Which leaves room for these rates to come down if and as the fundamentals materialize and for IG borrowers to try the same trade on even better terms.

Eight months of silence. Time to explain why…
 
I stopped posting on X because everything had become too noisy, especially in crypto.
 
When everyone is financially incentivized to post, the signal-to-noise ratio inevitably collapses. Engagement farming takes over. And at times, especially when prices are falling and everything becomes PvP, sharing real ideas starts to feel less worthwhile.
 
Sometimes the best thing you can do is step away and simply observe for a while.
 
And that’s exactly what I did.
 
I made a choice to put all my effort and focus into the people who subscribed to our research.
 
At GMI and @RealVision, I kept publishing. In fact, leaving X for a bit allowed me to produce some of the best and most original macro work of my career.
 
Removing myself from the noise turned out to be one of the best things I could have done, because it gave me back something I had been missing: time to think.
 
There were personal reasons too…
 
My third daughter arrived, and there is nothing quite like having a newborn at home to put the rest of life into perspective.
 
I also turn 40 this year. A milestone birthday has a way of doing the same thing. It makes you stop, take stock, and look hard at what you want from the next chapter.

And the truth is, what I wanted from the past decade of my life is not what I want from the next one.
 
@RaoulGMI and I have spoken for years about the period beyond 2030: a time when entirely new ways of thinking, working, and living emerge. 
 
If we’re even half right about what lies ahead, then I know exactly what I want from the next decade…
 
Whatever I build next, I want control. Over the direction. Over the product. And most importantly, over my time.
 
Because time is the real currency of life.
 
The need to take control of mine has been circling in my mind for years. I have finally decided to act on it.
 
So here is the change…
 
I have decided to step away from GMI and @RealVision to build something of my own. 
 
I’ll be launching my own macro research platform.
 
I won’t oversell it before it’s ready. But I know this much: it will be the most ambitious and comprehensive macro and investment framework I have ever built, and I’m incredibly excited about it.
 
More on this in Q4.
 
Now for the part that means the most to me…
 
@RaoulGMI, thank you.
 
For the trust, the friendship, and the opportunity to spend the past several years working together. It has been an important chapter in my career, and one I will always look back on with fondness and gratitude.
 
To everyone at @RealVision and GMI who made the work possible, week after week and month after month, thank you.
 
And most of all, thank you to the community…
 
Your questions made my research sharper. Your challenges made me think harder. You engaged with the ideas at a level I have rarely seen anywhere else, and you reminded me constantly why this work is worth doing.
 
Of everything I accomplished over the past few years, nothing means more to me than the friendships I made along the way.
 
The next couple of months are for my family and for building what comes next.
 
But i’ll be around, sharing ideas and perspectives whenever I have something worth saying.
 
In the meantime, enjoy the rest of your summer everyone...
